items.title: Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1
items.why_it_matters: Anthropic has released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, their latest model updates. As someone who relies heavily on Claude to write your code, any major model update directly impacts your development speed and code quality. This week, you can update your Claude Code configuration or your Next.js API endpoints to use the new `claude-fable-5-1` model and see if it handles your Next.js routing and Supabase queries with fewer errors.

items.title: Show HN: Lanes, simple Claude coordination that exploits 0.1x cache-read pricing
items.why_it_matters: Lanes is a new open-source tool designed to coordinate Claude API calls while maximizing Anthropic's 0.1x prompt caching discount. Because you are building AI-ingest, keeping your API costs low is crucial for making your project financially viable. This week, you can clone the Lanes repository and use it to structure your AI-ingest backend calls to take advantage of Anthropic's cheap prompt caching.

items.title: Hermes, Claude Code, and Codex ran an identical model. Token use varied 70-fold
items.why_it_matters: A new benchmark shows that different agent harnesses (like Claude Code and Codex) running the exact same model can vary up to 70-fold in token consumption. Since you use both tools and want to keep your development costs down, understanding how they consume tokens is highly valuable. This week, you can review your Claude Code terminal logs to see if your agent is getting stuck in expensive loops, and try limiting its context window to save tokens.

items.title: ModelGate – Find repetitive and expensive LLM calls in your back end
items.why_it_matters: ModelGate is an open-source tool designed to detect and block repetitive, expensive LLM calls in your backend. When building AI-ingest, a bug in your loop logic could easily drain your API balance overnight. This week, you can integrate ModelGate into your Next.js API routes to automatically flag and block duplicate or runaway Claude API requests in your dev environment.

items.title: Claude Code setup I built for a bike workshop's 20-year-old classic ASP system
items.why_it_matters: A developer shared their custom Claude Code setup used to successfully refactor a massive legacy system. Seeing how others configure Claude Code for real-world production work gives you a direct blueprint for optimizing your own workflow. This week, you can read their configuration file to see how they structured their environment, and copy their custom rules into your own project's `.claudecode` config.

items.title: Show HN: Open-sourced runtime for better Codex and Claude subagent experience
items.why_it_matters: This is an open-source runtime built specifically to improve the subagent experience when using Codex and Claude. If you find yourself struggling with agents losing context or failing on multi-step tasks, this runtime offers a more structured way to manage them. This week, you can clone the repo and run their demo to see if this subagent runtime handles multi-file refactoring tasks better than your current Codex setup.
